title: PDF Agenda for Town Council Regular Meeting - 11/10/2026 - 9:00am
text: TOWN COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING 21 Main Street Tuesday, November 10, 2026 at 9:00 AM AGENDA Possible additions to the agenda and related materials are not set forth herein. Times set forth are approximate and may be adjusted as necessary. I. WORKSESSION - 9:00 AM A. Snow Removal Program Overview Staff will provide an overview of the Town’s snow removal program in advance of the upcoming winter season. The presentation will include information on ongoing preparations, typical operations, resident expectations, and related Town Code regulations. The presentation is intended to prepare Town Council and the community for the upcoming snow season and answer common questions about the service. No Council action is requested. Presenter: John Ward, Public Works Director. B. 45 Winchester Street: Property Maintenance Enforcement History and Proposed Corrective Action Staff will provide an overview of the history of property maintenance and building code enforcement at 45 Winchester Street, including complaints, inspections, notices of violation, court proceedings, and efforts to obtain compliance. The presentation will provide background for Town Council's consideration of appropriating funds to correct outstanding violations on the privately owned property. A public hearing is scheduled to be held for the appropriation of funds at the Regular Meeting. Presenters: Hunter Digges, Building Official, and Rob Walton, Director of Community Development. C. Ordinance 2026-14: Town Code Amendment Regarding Commercial Refuse Collection Outside the Historic District. Town Council will continue discussion on an amendment to Section 8-21 of the Town Code that would discontinue Town-provided refuse collection for commercial properties outside the Historic District. Staff will present updated information in advance of the Public Hearing which will be continued at the Regular Meeting. Presenter: Lauren Kruck, Project Manager. D. Nonprofit Organization Amusement Device Permit and Inspection Fees Staff will present potential policy changes regarding amusement device permit and inspection fees for nonprofit organizations, including options for administrative fee waivers, reimbursements, or reduced fees. Council will be asked to provide direction on whether to pursue amendments to the Town Code or fee schedule to establish a consistent process for qualifying nonprofit organizations. Presenter: Rob Walton, Community Development Director. E. Memorandum of Agreement with Fauquier County for Use of Town Hall Staff will present a revised Memorandum of Agreement with Fauquier County providing for continued use of Town Hall at 21 Main Street for County offices and public meetings. The agreement maintains Town ownership and control of the facility and authorizes the Town Manager to execute and administer the agreement on behalf of the Town. This item is placed on the Regular Meeting agenda for consideration by Town Council. Presenter: Judson Rex, Town Manager. F. Revised Operational Use and Management Agreement with NPSC Staff will present a revised Operational Use and Management Agreement with the Northern Piedmont Sports Club (NPSC) providing for the continued use of the athletic fields at the Warrenton Sports Complex. The agreement maintains Town ownership and oversight of the Sports Complex and authorizes the Town Manager to execute and administer the agreement on behalf of the Town. Staff is seeking input from the Town Council on the proposed agreement before it is placed on a future Regular Meeting agenda for formal consideration. Presenter: Kelly Koernig, Parks and Recreation Director. G. Retail Cannabis Sales: Zoning Regulations and Potential Town Code Amendments. Staff will brief Town Council on changes to Virginia law authorizing adultuse retail cannabis sales beginning July 1, 2027, and discuss potential amendments to the Town Code and Zoning Ordinance to regulate retail cannabis establishments, including applicable zoning requirements and local taxation options. Council will be asked to provide direction on whether to initiate the development of proposed regulations for future consideration. Presenters: Rob Walton, Director of Community Development, and Heather Jenkins, Zoning Administrator. H. Town Council Resolution Regarding Committees Town Council will consider a resolution confirming the Council’s role in creating Town committees, appointing their members and the Town’s representatives to outside bodies, and directing staff support for them, including designation of the Town’s representatives to the Town/County Liaison Committee. The resolution is on the Regular Meeting agenda under New Business. Presenter: Mr. Judson Rex, Town Manager I. Discussion of a Proposed Town Council Transportation Committee At the request of Councilmember Larry Kovalik, Town Council will discuss the potential establishment of a transportation committee to review and address transportation needs and priorities within the Town of Warrenton. Presenter: Larry Kovalik, Ward 3 Councilmember. J. Finance Committee Update Committee Chair, Bill Semple, Ward 2 will provide an update on items discussed at recent Finance Committee Meetings. Committee Members: Bill Semple, Ward 2 (Chair) and Paul Mooney, At-large. Staff Liaison: Stephanie Miller, Director of Finance K. Public Safety Committee Update Committee Chair, Michele O'Halloran, Ward 4 will provide an update on items discussed at recent Public Safety Committee Meetings. Committee Members: Michele O'Halloran, Ward 4 (Chair) and David McGuire, At-large. Staff Liaison: Tim Carter, Police Chief. L. Agenda Review Staff will provide an overview of the 6:30 p.m. Regular Meeting agenda and provide Town Council an opportunity to raise questions, comments, or requested changes. Presenter: Judson Rex, Town Manager M. Closed Session The Town Council will meet in Closed Session to discuss topics allowed under the Virginia Freedom of Information Act. II. REGULAR MEETING - 6:30 PM A. INVOCATION. B. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE. C. PROCLAMATIONS AND RECOGNITIONS. D. CITIZEN'S TIME. E. APPROVAL OF THE AGENDA. F. PUBLIC HEARINGS. a. Ordinance 2026-14: Town Code Amendment Regarding Commercial Refuse Collection Outside the Historic District. Town Council will continue discussion on an amendment to Section 8-21 of the Town Code that would discontinue Town-provided refuse collection for commercial properties outside the Historic District. Staff will present updated information in advance of the Public Hearing which will be continued at the Regular Meeting. Presenter: Lauren Kruck, Project Manager. b. A RESOLUTION TO AMEND THE FISCAL YEAR 2027 ADOPTED BUDGET TO APPROPRIATEFUND BALANCE IN THE AMOUNT OF $636,560.00 TO FUND IMPROVEMENTS REQUIRED TO ABATE PROPERTY MAINTENANCE VIOLATIONS ASSOCIATED WITH ENFC23-73 AT 45 WINCHESTER STREET. This proposed budget amendment would appropriate fund balance in the amount of $636,560.00 for physical improvements associated with ENFC-23-73 and required to abate property maintenance violations at 45 Winchester Street. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY This Snow Removal presentation is to include but is not limited to: Phases of Deployment, Shifts, Equipment, and Expectations of both Staff and Citizens. BACKGROUND During inclement weather our Public Works first responders are deployed. It is our department that ensures roadways are safe, clear, and passable for emergency vehicles, citizens, and visitors, as well. The severity of the storm interprets what plan of action is necessary for our crews to make the roadways safe. Twelve-hour shifts are implemented in severe weather cases. Winter storms place a substantial operational strain on our equipment. STAFF RECOMMENDATION Town Staff would recommend citizens to stay alert because weather warnings and snow emergency enforcement be in place. Page 2 ATTACHMENTS 1. Snow Removal Presentation 8 Item A. TOPIC/SNOW REMOVAL Town Council Regular Meeting November 10th, 2026 9 REPORT OVERVIEW Item A. • The department is responsible for clearing over 100 lane miles of roadway during winter weather events. • Severe Weather Shift Schedules To ensure continuous coverage during a severe weather event, operations transition into two 12hour shifts: • Day Shift: 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM • Night Shift: 7:00 PM – 7:00 AM • Staffing per Shift: Each shift is staffed by 8 drivers operating 8 designated trucks and plows. • Phased Equipment Deployment Equipment utilization changes based on the active storm phase: • Phases 1 through 3: Full deployment of all available trucks, spreaders, and plows to maintain primary roadways. • Phase 4: Drivers transition out of standard trucks to operate heavy machinery, including loaders with plows, backhoes, skid steers, and the John Deere tractor. • We use approximately 600 tons of salt per winter. This does not include the sand/salt mixture. 11/10/2026 TOPIC/SNOW REMOVAL 2 10 SNOW PREPARATION Item A. • October marks the start of winter storm preparations for the Fleet and Public Works Departments, focusing on equipment readiness, route training, and strategic scheduling. • During this period, teams complete several key tasks: • Equipment Prepped: Technicians clean, test, and tune up all trucks, snowplows, and spreaders to ensure they are service-ready. • Materials Stocked: Crews audit and replenish the inventory of de-icing chemicals and abrasives. • Route Rehearsals: New drivers take their assigned trucks—complete with plows attached—out to memorize and familiarize themselves with their designated routes. • Shift Optimization: The Superintendent and Senior Crew Supervisor finalize the staff and equipment schedules to maximize operational efficiency and coverage. 11/10/2026 TOPIC/SNOW REMOVAL 3 11 SNOW PREP PICTURES 11/10/2026 TOPIC/SNOW REMOVAL Item A. 4 12 SNOW REMOVAL PHASES Item A. PHASE I: Salt Spreader trucks treating and/or pre-treating at the beginning to early stage of the storm (snow or ice). They treat with salt all arterial roads as needed, up to 1½” of accumulation of snow or ice. PHASE II: When salt is no longer efficient or effective, plow trucks are deployed to their assigned routes. (It is likely during this phase that sanitation routes will be delayed or cancelled as 12-hour shifts are designated and put into effect requiring sanitation staff to fill in on snow routes) PHASE III: When all arterial roads have been plowed and the storm allows, trucks then will be deployed into subdivisions, side streets and parking lots. At this time, the storm will be evaluated to determine if salt needs to be reapplied or other means of treatment is necessary. 11/10/2026 TOPIC/SNOW REMOVAL 5 13 SNOW REMOVAL PHASES Item A. PHASE IV: At this phase it means that it is continuing to snow and our regular equipment is no longer able to keep up with the heavy snow. Small plow trucks will be pulled off, and we will designate all heavy equipment to arterial roads to work as a team of two to maintain and keep the arterial roads passable. (During this phase sanitation crews will be moved into operation positions and will be plowing snow) After every major storm, (over 8”), all efforts shift to Main St. snow removal. Spreaders are removed from dump trucks, and they are used to haul all snow from Main Street to make it safe and passable. 11/10/2026 TOPIC/SNOW REMOVAL 6 14 SNOW REMOVAL PHASES Item A. • In the past, before during or after any storm, the Superintendent or designated person may call on additional rental equipment and or operators if he feels it will be necessary to assist in spreading, plowing or hauling throughout the storm to keep the roadways passable and safe, however, due to budget restraints this provision has been suspended at this time. • If significant inclement weather occurs having this resource suspended will hinder the efficiency of opening the streets in a timely manner and getting businesses and citizens back to normal routine. 11/10/2026 TOPIC/SNOW REMOVAL 7 15 SNOW REMOVAL PICTURES 11/10/2026 TOPIC/SNOW REMOVAL Item A. 8 16 SNOW REMOVAL PICTURES 11/10/2026 TOPIC/SNOW REMOVAL Item A. 9 17 Item A. SNOW REMOVAL MAP SNOW REMOVAL MAP • The snow removal areas listed are designed to deploy Town units to remove snow from subdivisions and side streets. The map has 7 areas that are numbered and color coded. • Each area has the same priority in snow removal. The exception being if a 911 emergency call came in. At that time, the location/street would take high priority to make it accessible and assist emergency vehicles get to destination. • NOTE: The white area of map is mainly Old Town area. We have one unit specifically designated for that area during snow/ice storms. 11/10/2026 TOPIC/SNOW REMOVAL 10 18 Item A. TOWN CODE SNOW REMOVAL MAP • Sec. 14-5. - Removal of snow and ice. • modified • (a) • Removal required. Every occupant, owner, or other person in charge of any occupied property in the town which has a sidewalk or footway of stone, brick, gravel, cinder, wood, or other substance, when such sidewalk is publicly owned or maintained, shall have all snow and ice removed within twenty-four (24) hours after such snow or ice ceases falling. For accumulations of more than six (6) inches, the removal window shall be extended to forty-eight (48) hours after precipitation ceases. When a property is unoccupied, this duty falls upon the owner or the agent of the owner. 11/10/2026 TOPIC/SNOW REMOVAL 11 19 Item A. The settlement would resolve claims against Albertsons concerning its alleged misconduct in the distribution and dispensing of opioids. It requires Albertsons to pay^B^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^B, including approximately | for participating states and subdivisions to address the impacts of the opioid crisis. It also requires changes to Albertsons' opioid dispensing practices and safeguards intended to prevent the diversion of prescription opioids. Participation is open to eligible subdivisions within participating states, whether or not they previously filed a lawsuit against Albertsons. Greater subdivision participation increases the funding available to a state and its subdivisions. A subdivision that does not participate cannot directly share in the settlement funds, even if its state participates. Because the amount your subdivision may receive will depend on settlement participation, unfortunately we cannot provide a confirmed payment amount for your subdivision at this time.
